history.prompt: On a brushed-steel workbench in a machine shop, a compact matte clay metering assembly: three graphite tally-register modules in a row on a cast aluminum baseplate. A single flanged input rail enters from the left and splits into three short branch lanes, each leading to one module. The first module has an open safety-yellow gate that also counts a side handoff chute; the second has a one-way ratchet gate blocking the side chute; the third has no gate, a flat pass-through slot. Tiny blank count dials, moulding seams, and contact shadows. One directional key light rakes from the upper left, throwing long cast shadows. Bone white, graphite, safety yellow. Asymmetric off-centre composition, wide 16:9.

style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression in a data hall corridor: three brushed-steel turnstile gates recede diagonally, each gate fitted with a different mechanical metering register and a latch set at a different handoff angle. Hard directional light rakes from the left across the steel, throwing long shadows on the concrete floor; graphite, safety yellow, bone white. Perforated metal rear wall, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos. Extreme asymmetric framing with the nearest gate off-centre right.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, distorted characters
rationale: The article is about three vendors' metering definitions colliding at the handoff. A compressed telephoto row of turnstile gates in a data hall gives the scale and repetitive industrial rhythm of pricing machinery, while each gate's metering register shows a different billable event, avoiding a sterile spreadsheet or product shot.
subject: three turnstile gates in a data hall corridor, each with a different mechanical metering register and a latch at a different handoff position
core_thesis: AI vendors moved from selling seats to selling units, and each writes the unit's own definition on its pricing page, so one handled customer request is priced from $0.20 to $2.00 and the definition sentence is the term to negotiate, not the rate.
core_conflict: Vendor-written unit definitions versus the buyer's cost per resolved task; handoffs to a human, silent customers, and same-day returns each bill differently under Intercom, Zendesk, and Salesforce wording.
composition: extreme asymmetric framing with the nearest gate off-centre right and three gates receding diagonally in compressed telephoto layers
